sentences.text: The regional service divides its operating area into defined response zones so dispatch decisions reflect distance, road access, and available ambulance capacity.
Zone boundaries are maintained with participating jurisdictions and reviewed when road networks, population patterns, or service agreements change.
Each zone has primary and alternate routes to the Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center, subject to clinical direction and current access conditions.
Dispatch personnel consider travel time, road restrictions, weather, and known closures when selecting a route or estimating arrival times.
Access conditions can change rapidly around hospitals, bridge approaches, and controlled entry points, so crews verify conditions before committing to a constrained route.
The North Gate Status Board presents current access and queue conditions for the northern approach.
The South Gate Status Board presents current access conditions for the southern approach, including restrictions that may affect ambulance entry.
Both gate boards are checked at shift start and whenever a reported access change could affect response or hospital arrival.
The North Gate Status Board produces the North Approach Queue Snapshot for use in maintaining an up-to-date view of northern approach congestion.
The Radio Coordinator is also known as Mistral in operational communications.
The Radio Coordinator monitors the Regional Radio Network and helps maintain clear communications among dispatch personnel and ambulance crews.
The Radio Coordinator confirms that assigned channels are available and that backup communications procedures are understood at the start of each shift.
Radio checks verify coverage in known weak-signal areas and identify equipment or network problems before demand rises.
The Fleet Maintenance Cell is also known as Bluejay in operational communications.
The Fleet Maintenance Cell monitors vehicle availability, scheduled servicing, and reported defects that could reduce zone coverage.
The Fleet Maintenance Cell produces the Battery Swap Voucher to document an authorized battery replacement.
Readiness checks confirm that each available ambulance has suitable staffing, functioning communications equipment, and required clinical supplies.
The checks also confirm fuel status, vehicle condition, and any maintenance restrictions recorded for the unit.
The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
